A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and algorithms. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial revisions and reformatting.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original cumulative-regret experiments on Forrester, CIFAR-10 hyperparameter optimization, and Lunar Lander.

after.justification: Section 5 retains original Forrester results and reports revised CIFAR-10 and Lunar Lander results, including averages and uncertainty across seeds.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 replace the unobservable clean-data standard deviation in acquisition with the observable RCGP standard deviation multiplied by a new factor, Psi(Tc). The adaptive model's plateau width also incorporates this factor. These change the formal selection and weighting procedures, while retaining the underlying P-IMQ and anchor/adaptive architecture.

E1.justification: The three benchmark tasks remain unchanged, but the Lunar Lander corruption scenario changes from falsely high rewards of +1000 to falsely low rewards of -1000. This revises the adversarial observation conditions within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: GP-UCB, Student-t Process UCB, and DiagnosticsGP remain the evaluated comparators in the corresponding experiments. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: CIFAR-10 changes from 150 to 140 BO iterations, 4 to 10 initial points, and 2 to 4 training epochs per evaluation. Lunar Lander changes from 800 to 300 iterations, 5 to 10 initial points, and 5 to 4 episodes per evaluation. The appendix's Forrester iteration setting also changes from 25 to 30, although its plots remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The Lunar Lander robustness test is revised to assess resistance to spuriously low rewards instead of deceptive high rewards, with replacement evidence in Figure 5. No separate component ablations or systematic parameter-sensitivity studies are added.

E5.justification: V1 describes CIFAR-10 using a shared random seed; v2 explicitly repeats it across ten seeds and reports means and standard errors. Lunar Lander also newly reports ten-seed aggregation and standard errors. This substantially extends uncertainty reporting beyond Forrester, whose ten-run reporting is retained.

E6.justification: Figures 4–5 contain replacement results under revised settings. The CIFAR-10 curves now place FC-RCGP and A2-RCGP nearly together. In Lunar Lander, Student-t and DiagnosticsGP finish below GP in mean cumulative regret, reversing their earlier ordering relative to GP, despite retained prose saying otherwise. These are not same-setting performance gains. Forrester results in Figures 1 and 3 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds variance-comparison and observable-confidence-bound Lemmas 5–7 and substantially revises both regret derivations. Assumption 3 becomes a high-probability function bound, and the analysis retains previously suppressed beta-prime dependence. The thinned-clean-data construction is removed. New Appendix E compares observable and ideal corruption budgets, while Appendix H derives a standard GP's sensitivity to a single corruption.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions narrow the advertised corruption tolerance from O(T^(1/2)) and O(T^(1/3)) to O(T^(1/4)) and O(T^(1/7)) for FC-RCGP-UCB and A2-RCGP-UCB, respectively. The introduction now distinguishes empirical robustness at T^(1/3) from the weaker guarantees. The zero-cost robustness claim remains.

C2.justification: Sections 4.3 and 5.6 newly interpret the gap between empirical corruption tolerance and proven rates as suggesting a loose observability penalty. The discussion also explicitly identifies known corruption budgets and function bounds as theoretical limitations and discusses robustness to misspecifying them. The Tc=0 heuristic observation already appeared in v1's appendix.

D1.justification: V2 updates experimental configuration listings, explains the base-seed-plus-run-index convention, and discloses using the heuristic function bound sqrt(Bf*kappa)=1. Embedded code links change repository identifiers from RCGP-943C to RCGP-46DE. Hardware, software, execution instructions, and runtime descriptions are otherwise retained; external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: V2 adds Li and Luo (2026), distinguishing their tempered-posterior treatment of model misspecification from this work's outlier robustness. It removes the Byzantine-failure reference to Blanchard et al. (2017). The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites of acquisition-function explanations, theoretical qualifications, and discussion, plus corrected cross-references and reorganized appendix subsections. The acknowledgments are removed. The main narrative sequence and much of the existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from two columns to one, relocating figures and widening algorithm and theorem displays. Figures 4–5 are redrawn with uncertainty bands and revised axis ranges, and Appendix E adds Table 1. Figures 1–3 retain their original graphical content.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the central theoretical contribution by supplying an observable-variance bound and revising the algorithms and claims to account for its cost, addressing v1's dependence on unavailable clean-data variance. Ten-seed uncertainty reporting also strengthens both application evaluations. These gains outweigh reporting shortcomings: Appendix I retains stale variance-proxy reasoning, and Section 5.5 contradicts Figure 5's revised baseline ordering.
